text.p: German drugs group Schering AG said on Monday it was actively looking to make an acquisition to underpin growth in its therapeutics business unit.
"Our goal is to strengthen the therapeutics division, and we are actively looking in this area," Schering chief executive Giuseppe Vita told a news conference.
But he said finding a suitable partner or target was difficult as there are not very many innovative companies active in this sector. He gave no timeframe for when a takeover may be made.
"There are not very many innovative groups in this area, and we are not willing to pay any price" for a cooperation deal or takeover, Vita added.

This year Schering, the world's largest maker of oral contraceptives, paid about one billion marks for acquisitions of German fertility control group Jenapharm and Finnish gynaecology group Leiras, Schering said.

Additionally Schering's crop protection unit AgrEvo, which is runs as a 40/60 joint venture with Hoechst AG, paid about one billion marks for the acquisition of Plant Genetics Systems, Schering chief financial officer Klaus Pohle said.
Schering's mulitple sclerosis drug Betaseron, marketed under the name Betaferon in Europe, is the group's best known and most successful product in the therapeutics area.
In addition to its therapeutics unit, Schering has a fertility control and hormone therapy unit and a diagnostics business as well as a smaller dermatology unit.
